title: Recommended Childhood and Adolescent Immunization Schedule: United States, 2026: Policy Statement
summary:
AAP released its 2026 pediatric schedule on January 26, retaining routine protection against 18 diseases; the associated Pediatrics policy appeared February 9. This is society guidance, not a new efficacy trial. The release preserved AAP’s existing routine recommendations despite differences from federal guidance, including hepatitis A/B, influenza, rotavirus and meningococcal vaccination.

AAP’s release summary recommends COVID-19 vaccination for children aged 6–23 months and specified older risk groups, and permits access for families seeking protection. It retains a two-dose HPV approach beginning at ages 9–12 years and allows either separate MMR/varicella or MMRV for the first toddler dose. These are historical release recommendations; consult the maintained schedule for subsequent changes.
findings: Use age, catch-up interval and medical-condition tables together with product-specific notes; delayed series generally do not require restarting.
The policy adds clesrovimab, updates COVID-19 and HPV presentation, and adds combined meningococcal-product contraindications; these changes do not constitute a new comparative trial.
Later correction: February 5 addendum changes a Table 3 HIV CD4 column threshold from <200/mm³ to ≥200/mm³.
Later September revisions include MenACWY-TT minimum age, seasonal COVID-19/influenza information, RSV risk/repeat-dose criteria and maternal RSV timing. Do not attribute those revisions to January.

Before administration, distinguish anaphylaxis contraindications from precautions and consult the complete product-specific appendix. For example, rotavirus contraindications include SCID and prior intussusception.
comparator: Prior AAP schedule and contemporaneous federal recommendations; no randomized comparison.
population: US infants, children and adolescents aged 18 years or younger; pregnancy and risk-condition notes apply where specified.
shortTitle: AAP 2026 immunization schedule: retain routine protection; check dated updates

corrections.description: Official schedule addendum corrects the Table 3 HIV CD4 column threshold; this record links the maintained corrected schedule.
Retrieved PDF bears this update date and lists September 1 substantive revisions; historical January guidance is distinguished from later updates.

limitations: Official release summary and selected schedule notes, appendix and addendum reviewed; comprehensive vaccine-by-vaccine evidence appraisal was not performed. The accessible 19-page PDF is updated September 2, rather than the original January file. Direct policy retrieval redirected to login; indexed official policy text was inspected.
intervention: AAP age-based and risk-based immunization schedule, catch-up tables and contraindication/precaution appendix.
whyItMatters: During ED counseling or catch-up referrals, identify which organization’s schedule is being used and reconcile immunization records with the dated tables, notes and contraindications. This summary does not replace an exposure-specific prophylaxis protocol.
evidenceNotes: Release date verified in official AAP News https://publications.aap.org/aapnews/news/34141/ and the PDF addendum. Policy DOI/PMID identify the later companion paper, not a February first release of the schedule. Official IDSA endorsement https://www.idsociety.org/practice-guideline/recommended-childhood-and-adolescent-immunization-schedule-united-states-2026-policy-statement/ confirms February 9 paper date and evidence-to-recommendations framework. Performed DOI correction/retraction and official November-update searches; no separate notice established from returned material. The maintained PDF itself documents superseding changes. Individual vaccine effects, certainty and regulatory status were not independently reappraised.
primaryEndpoint: Recommended immunization timing and safe implementation; no new trial endpoint or pooled effect estimate.
guidelineStrength: AAP policy informed by evidence-to-recommendations review; no uniform GRADE strength or certainty assigned to this entire schedule. Do not infer identical evidence strength across vaccines.
